scope: What ClawX can and cannot do towards recursive self-improvement, recorded per capability layer and per evidence level. A planning artefact is not counted as a capability at any level.
claimBoundary: This matrix records the current state of the system. It does not claim that any capability here produces a benefit, and it does not authorize enabling anything.

evidenceLevels.source: Implementation bytes are present in product source and reachable from a real entry point.
evidenceLevels.engineering: A checked-in test, contract check or static gate exercises the implementation.
evidenceLevels.runtime: A real Electron, Gateway or OpenClaw runtime path consumed the implementation and left a receipt.
evidenceLevels.effect: The user-visible journey reached its requested end state, with a negative control and a recovery or rollback receipt.
evidenceLevels.not-run: Nothing was executed at this level. Recorded explicitly so an unrun level can never be read as a pass.

layers.title: Experience loop (SEKB)
layers.summary: ClawX captures agent trajectories, distils candidate principles, requires an explicit confirmation before a durable write, retrieves confirmed principles, and has a typed but unwired adoption counter. Default off, no automatic write-back.

defaultState.schemaDefault: none; the zod leaf at openclaw_runtime/src/config/zod-schema.ts is optional with no default, so an absent setting resolves to false
defaultState.readMeCarefully: openclaw_runtime/src/config/runtime-feature-leaves.ts sets sekb.enabled to true, but that file is a compile-checked type/zod parity sample, not a runtime default. Its own header says every leaf needs one sample value; it must never be read as the product default.

stages.label: Capture agent trajectories

source.note: Harness hooks start, step and finish a trajectory; the host exposes the capture route.

engineering.note: Unit coverage exists for the capture and no-auto-writeback boundaries.

runtime.note: Reached in an Electron host-api E2E run. The hooks are only installed when the SEKB runtime resolved, which requires the master flag, so a default configuration captures nothing.

effect.note: No product run with SEKB enabled recorded a captured trajectory feeding a later user-visible outcome.

limitations: Off by default, so the default product configuration exercises no capture path.
The in-app capture entry point is a manual, typed input; it is not the same mechanism as automatic trajectory capture.

stages.label: Distil candidate principles

source.note: Deterministic suggestion path; an optional batch assistant path is separately flagged off.

runtime.note: Exercised through the typed host-api workflow in an Electron E2E fixture. The fixture itself is labelled engineering-validation-only.

effect.note: No live-provider distillation run and no product-benefit evidence has been recorded.

limitations: Suggestions are advisory and mutation-free by rule; producing a suggestion is not an improvement.

stages.label: Explicit confirmation and durable write

source.note: Confirmation is the only durable principle write path and carries provenance.

engineering.note: Provenance and the no-auto-writeback boundary are unit-covered.

runtime.note: Electron host-api E2E recorded the confirm step persisting a block with a read-back receipt.

effect.note: The golden-path evidence records a behaviour delta after confirmation. It is an E2E fixture run, so it shows the loop closes inside the harness; it is not product-benefit evidence.

limitations: Requires an explicit actor action; there is no automatic path into a durable write.
The recorded effect comes from a fixture-driven run, not a user journey.

stages.label: Retrieve confirmed principles

source.note: Ranked retrieval over confirmed principles, with a retrieval counter.

engineering.note: Ranking and counter behaviour are unit-covered.

runtime.note: Recall step recorded in the Electron E2E golden path.

effect.note: Retrieval is advisory by rule: the surface displays the injection text and does not attach it. No product journey has been shown to change because of a retrieved principle.

limitations: harness/specs/rules/sekb-assisted-review-boundary.md forbids the UI from attaching retrieved text automatically, so retrieval cannot by itself produce an effect.

stages.label: Record adoption and outcome

source.note: The store method and its persisted schema exist and validate their trigger vocabulary.

engineering.note: Unit tests call the method directly.

runtime.note: A whole-repository search finds no production caller of record_adoption; every caller is a test. There is therefore no runtime signal that flips cited, adopted or outcome, and the persisted adoption count stays at zero in product. The read-only surface that displays it is a dead read.

effect.note: Adoption cannot be observed because nothing records it.

limitations: The adoption stage is wired only to tests. Reporting an adoption rate from this system today would be reporting an untriggered counter.
Ranking logic that consumes the adoption count consequently degrades to its tie-break.

automaticWriteBack.statement: No automatic path writes a knowledge entry back into agent behaviour, a prompt file, a skill, a harness spec or product source code.
automaticWriteBack.nearestExistingMechanism: A flag-gated, per-turn prompt and tool-result injection that appends confirmed principle text during context assembly. It assembles a turn; it writes no file and is off by default.

layerLimitations: Default off, so nothing in this layer is exercised by a default configuration.
The loop is a reviewed suggestion pipeline, not a self-improvement loop: no stage changes the agent's own instructions without an explicit actor action.

layers.title: Harness self-modification
layers.summary: The system generating, evaluating and landing changes to its own harness — prompts, specs, rules, gates, skills or agent configuration — does not exist.

defaultState.note: There is no flag, because there is no capability to flag.

stages.label: Generate a candidate harness change

source.note: No code generates a candidate harness, prompt, spec or rule change.

limitations: resources/skills/preinstalled/self-improving-agent/ is a bundled third-party skill that a human invokes to log a learning. It is a static resource, is not wired to any loop, and does not generate or land harness changes.

stages.label: Evaluate a harness candidate against a frozen gate

engineering.note: No test covers a capability that does not exist.

limitations: The measurement instruments this would need are recorded under measurementSubstrate below. Instruments are not a capability.

stages.label: Land or roll back a harness candidate automatically

source.note: No automatic merge, apply or rollback path for a self-generated harness change.

limitations: The only change paths into harness/specs/** are a human-driven authoring flow and test fixtures that write into temporary roots.

layerLimitations: The absence is verified by search, not by a gate: there is no test asserting that self-modification is absent, so this row is a recorded observation with the search scope stated.
No ACE, ReasoningBank, SICA, DGM, Darwin Godel, OpenEvolve or AlphaEvolve reference exists anywhere in the repository.

layers.title: Code self-modification
layers.summary: The system generating, evaluating and merging changes to its own product source code does not exist.

defaultState.note: There is no flag, because there is no capability to flag.

stages.label: Generate a candidate code change

source.note: No self-patch, candidate-diff or patch-generation loop exists.

limitations: Agent-assisted coding is performed by an external coding agent under human review. That is assisted authoring, not the product modifying itself.

stages.label: Evaluate a code candidate against the frozen gate
Merge a self-generated code change

source.note: No automatic merge path for self-generated product code.

limitations: Self-healing code that exists is unrelated and bounded: gateway reconnect and config-migration repair, plus a versioned write journal with undo. None of them authors or merges new product behaviour.

layerLimitations: Stage 4 (TF-0602) is the only place this is allowed to be researched, and it requires stage 3 to land first.

measurementSubstrate.description: Instruments that a later RSI stage would measure with. Listed separately so they are never mistaken for RSI capability: an instrument that can measure an improvement is not an improvement.

items.note: pass^k and pass@k with k=3, a 20-complete-case floor, flake detection and insufficient-sample semantics.
Paired effect size with a 95 percent interval, latency percentiles, token counts, false blocks and safety violations.

The reliability fixture holds 5 cases at k=3 with only 4 complete and therefore reports insufficient-sample. The paired-ablation fixture holds 20 cases at k=3. Neither is a calibrated product task set.
The pass^k aggregation output directory artifacts/agent-dev-benefit-eval/ does not exist in this checkout, so no baseline aggregation has been run and recorded.
No production grader or judge service exists. Judge helpers exist only inside unit tests.
A Wilson interval at 0.95 and Cohen's kappa with frozen thresholds exist in the SEKB offline path. There is no bootstrap and no minimum-detectable-effect computation anywhere in the repository.

currentState.statement: ClawX has no complete recursive-self-improvement implementation.
whatExistsInstead: One flag-gated, human-confirmed experience loop (SEKB), default off.
Statistical aggregation and paired-ablation code with fixture-grade inputs only.
Planning and boundary documents for stages that have not been built.

prerequisites.rule: No candidate generation, harness self-modification or code self-modification may be implemented before the stage gate it depends on has landed with evidence.

limitations: Every row above is a recorded observation of source and artefact state, verified by reading files and searching the repository. It is not a test suite that fails when a capability appears.
Runtime and effect levels are marked not-run far more often than they are marked present; that asymmetry is the point of this matrix.
No benefit, promotion, default change, product-lock change, release decision or real-human claim is made anywhere in this fixture.
